head: efc3b24b0ede80c5561d15ece7e1f190d30a619a

retail_identity_check.conclusion: The active Binary Ninja view is the retail image, not the candidate: its entry point, image range and sampled code bytes match igi.exe.

scope: Manifest records whose implementation.path does not exist at HEAD because the legacy duplicate GameNatives filename was deleted from this branch.
finding: Every recorded implementation path is absent, but all 84 implementations exist in this branch under the canonical <address>-<Name>.cpp filename with byte-identical content (sha256 equal to implementation.sha256). The defect is a stale implementation.path, not missing candidate content. The records remain unbound to those files and are lowered to ANALYZED because no fresh verification was performed.
method: Enumerated every manifest record whose implementation.path is absent at HEAD (84 of 883).
Confirmed each path is absent in this worktree, then searched the branch for same-address .cpp files and compared their sha256 with implementation.sha256.
Located the recorded revision in git history and sibling worktrees.
Read the existing evidence artifacts and re-verified the retail Binary Ninja entry and CFG against the live Binary Ninja view of retail igi.exe.
Compared the radare2 artifact and the semantic-review artifacts against the Binary Ninja graph and their declared bindings.
Applied the status/limitation/historical-evidence patch in memory with RFC 7386 merge-patch semantics and compared aggregate statuses.
limitations: Retail entry and CFG were verified with the live Binary Ninja view; no fresh radare2 run was performed, so radare2 completeness is judged from the stored artifact.

The byte-identical same-address sources were deliberately not rebound to the records, because rebinding would require fresh per-native acceptance and would bypass the task instruction not to rebind to a convenient path.
No build, structural or runtime comparison was performed for the recorded revision in this branch.
The semantic-review artifacts are templated and are not usable as per-native candidate evidence.
